also_mentioned: MinAtar-style (said to resemble but not match any specific one)
marks.conclusion: A small policy or classifier for a procedurally generated 10x10x5 lane-like grid task; ch0 maybe the agent, ch1/ch4 objects in lanes repeating every 4 columns.
marks.judge_notes: Rulings where the rubric did not decide: (1) Channel meanings 2: ch0 as agent (supported by the central strip) and ch1 as objects in 4-apart lanes (supported by c/c+4 tying), both offered as the top-ranked reading, not as certainties; ch4 not read as previous frame. (2) Border 0: reply calls border/rows 0,1,9 'dead', not always-on; ch2/ch3 'dead' is said as 'probably always 0' so not deducted. (3) B_actions 0: 'e.g. no-op/up/down/left/right' is a hypothesis from the board layout, with no traced output meaning. (4) Depth level 1: traces h5/h6 to outputs but the conclusions cannot be confirmed (fact sheet: mechanism not traced). (5) Behaviour 0: 'lane-crossing policy' is named but what it does is not described. (6) Name bonus 0: it says it 'resembles MinAtar-style environments, but does not match any specific one' and ranks lane-crossing among options; I did not count that as committing. Another judge could give 2. (7) Activation: ReLU 'strongly' pointed to, wrong, 0. F_bonus_orientation does not apply (normal board).
